claim: The v0.10.0 utilization-detector saturation-detector plugin's implementation lives at a specific, citable Go source path: pkg/epp/framework/plugins/flowcontrol/saturationdetector/utilization/detector.go, lines 119-164, which fuses per-replica queue depth and KV-cache pressure into one pool-saturation signal.
stance_target: exact Go source location of a load-bearing flow-control plugin for chasing the plugin interface definition
quoted_support: The utilization detector combines per-replica queue and key-value (KV) cache pressure into one pool-saturation signal.

claim: Admission (Flow Control, deciding WHEN a request advances) and Scheduling (deciding WHERE it runs) are architecturally separate decisions inside the EPP: Flow Control fully completes -- evaluating priority bands high to low, applying a fairness policy then an ordering policy -- before backend Scheduling ever selects the highest-scored vLLM pod.
stance_target: clean separation of concerns between admission control and backend placement, relevant to isolating which layer needs changing for non-k8s backends
scope_conditions: llm-d EPP, v0.10.0-era flow control design
quoted_support: Admission and scheduling answer different questions. Admission determines when a request can advance. Scheduling determines where that admitted request should run.

claim: Priority is sourced from an InferenceObjective CRD that maps a workload to an integer (higher = higher priority); requests sharing a priority integer share a band and are arbitrated purely by the configured tenant fairness policy -- meaning the priority signal itself is a Kubernetes custom resource, another k8s-coupling point distinct from pod/metrics scraping.
stance_target: identifying InferenceObjective (a CRD) as a second, separate Kubernetes coupling point beyond pod-based endpoint discovery
quoted_support: An InferenceObjective maps a workload to an integer priority. Traffic is evaluated by an integer value; a higher value indicates higher-priority traffic.
